subject: general
question: If an object takes 2 seconds to travel once around a circular path with radius 'r', its speed 'v' is given by _______.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **circular motion**, distance covered in **one revolution** is the **circumference** = 2πr.

Speed v = Distance ÷ Time

v = 2πr ÷ 2

v = πr metre/sec

**∴ The correct answer is πr metre/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** of the circular path = r

**Time taken** for one revolution (T) = 2 seconds

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e30a9706d697de74e3a2cabf779c3ba5a6065e601aa92c54db93c919da43e42.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Speed (v) = Distance ÷ Time

In a circular path, **Distance** = **Circumference** = 2×π×Radius

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance = 2πr

⇒ v = (2πr) ÷ 2

⇒ v = πr metre/sec

**∴ The correct answer is πr metre/sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angular Velocity (ω)

It is the rate of change of angular displacement, ω = 2π/T. In this case, ω = 2π/2 = π rad/sec.

Relation between v and ω

Linear speed **v** is related to angular speed **ω** by the formula v = rω.

Centripetal Acceleration

For an object in uniform circular motion, acceleration a = v²/r = ω²r directed towards the center.</p
